text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The president approved the new cabinet of Prime Minister Mart Siimann with two new ministers - Education Minister Mait Klaassen and Agriculture Minister Andres Varik. Junior minister for Regional Affairs Tiit Kubri also resigned, but no replacement has been named.
- The Tallinna Pank will sell its 42.1 million kroon shipping loan to investment firm Talinvest.
- The Pensioners and Families Union, an electoral bloc within the ruling Coalition Party, called for a rise of the social tax to increase pensions.
- A sociological study from Tartu University shows students are convinced that their future depends on their own abilities.
- Estonian marathon runner Jane Salumae was first woman in the Rome marathon on Sunday with a time of 2:31.40.
- President Lennart Meri will visit Japan on March 19-26 and will open the Estonian embassy in Tokyo.
- The Tallinn municipality plans to sell 70 percent of the Tallinn Water Works; the city government recently decided to rise water rates by 40 percent.
